note: Literature indicates DEE119 shares overlapping neurodevelopmental and epileptic phenotypes with other DEEs and requires genome sequencing to diagnose non-coding snRNA variants.

evidence.text: Dominant RNU2-2-associated developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 119 highlights the necessity of genomic sequencing for neurodevelopmental and epileptic phenotypes.

source.title: Large Class of Neurodevelopmental Disorders Requires Genome Sequencing for Diagnosis
source.quote: dominant RNU2-2-associated developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 119 (MIM 621304)… the importance of genomic sequencing for neurodevelopmental and epileptic phenotypes.

evidence.text: Patients with RNU2-2 DEE presented with focal and generalized seizures, status epilepticus (5/5), severe to profound impairment, hyperventilation (3/5), sleep apnea (3/5), and hippocampal sclerosis (3/5), representing features overlapping with other severe epileptic encephalopathies.

source.title: Pathogenic Variants in RNU2‐2, a Non‐coding Spliceosomal RNA, Cause a Distinctive Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy
source.quote: Patients with RNU2-2 DEE had median seizure onset age of 24 months, focal and generalized seizures, status epilepticus (n = 5), severe to profound impairment, hyperventilation (n = 3), and obstructive sleep apnea (n = 3).

numbers.metric: recurrent pathogenic variants in unsolved DEE cohort
